title: By the kilo or by the piece

sections.title: Weigh it or count it
sections.content: Fruit and vegetables are weighed by the *kiló* or counted piece by piece. *Kiló* and *darab* work like *pohár*: the number and the measure come first, then the food, and the food takes the *-t*: *Két kiló paradicsomot kérek.* Single pieces can be counted directly, without *darab*: *Három banánt kérek.* The noun stays singular after a number.

items.english: I'd like two kilos of tomatoes.
I buy a kilo of pears.
We'd like a kilo of potatoes.

sections.content: After a vowel the *-t* goes straight on: *banánt*, *krumplit*; *körte* also lengthens its last vowel: *körtét*. *Paradicsom* needs a linking vowel: *paradicsomot*. Never put the *-t* on the measure: *kiló körtét*, not *kilót körte*.
